papers.title: Part 2 of a 2-part open-label clinical trial evaluating repeated nicotinamide riboside parenteral administration: 90 days of at-home subcutaneous injections
papers.abstract: Nicotinamide riboside (NR), a precursor to the essential coenzyme nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+), has been extensively studied following oral administration, while the longer-term safety and physiological effects of injectable NR remain less characterized. Following an initial in-clinic phase evaluating repeat intramuscular (IM) and subcutaneous (SC) administration of pharmaceutical-grade NR, participants transitioned to an at-home phase designed to assess the safety, feasibility, and exploratory physiological effects of repeated self-administered SC administration. Participants continued their assigned 50 or 100 mg dose group and self-administered NR subcutaneously 3 times weekly for approximately 90 days. Safety was assessed through adverse event (AE) monitoring, vital signs, and clinical laboratory health measures. Exploratory assessments included markers of mitochondrial bioenergetics, urinary biomarkers of oxidative stress, and participant-reported outcomes related to fatigue, sleep, pain, and quality of life. At-home administration of NR was generally well-tolerated, with no clear dose-dependent safety concerns identified over the study period. Further, participants were able to successfully self-administer repeated SC injections over the study period, demonstrating positive feasibility. Whole-blood NAD+ concentrations remained largely stable over time in both dose groups. MeScreen analysis demonstrated a reduction in GlycoATP at Day 30 and increases in the MitoATP/GlycoATP ratio at Day 30 and Day 90, signifying a preferential shift toward oxidative metabolism. These findings may be indicative of positive metabolic health shifts. Urinary oxidative stress profiling demonstrated heterogeneous temporal responses. Several lipid oxidation markers significantly declined at Day 30 but returned toward baseline at Day 90. Select markers of nucleic acid, nitrative stress, and advanced glycation end-product oxidation demonstrated more sustained reductions. These results for which the majority of measured oxidative stress markers improved suggest that NR injections may exhibit anti-oxidative characteristics. Validated participant-reported sleep and fatigue measures showed improvements. Self-reported facial skin improvement increased descriptively from 11.4% at baseline to 27.8% at Day 30 and 36.8% at Day 90; improvements noticed by others increased from 9.1% to 23.7%, while reported body-skin improvement increased more modestly, from 8.8% to 16.7%. As these outcomes were not designed or powered to establish efficacy or definitive clinical claims, the findings should be considered hypothesis generating and provide preliminary data to inform the selection of outcomes and design considerations for future randomized, placebo-controlled, adequately powered trials of SC NR administration.

papers.title: KNOWLEDGE OF METABOLIC SYNDROME, LIFESTYLE RISK BEHAVIOURS AND PREVENTIVE PRACTICES AMONG WOMEN ATTENDING KASOA POLYCLINIC, GHANA: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY.
papers.abstract: Background. Metabolic syndrome is a cluster of cardiometabolic risk factors that may increase the risk of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes, and African studies report a higher prevalence in women than in men. Prevention may depend, in part, on whether women recognise the condition and its modifiable risk factors. Relatively little appears to be known about this among women using primary-level health facilities in fast-growing peri-urban areas of Ghana. Objective. To assess knowledge of metabolic syndrome, describe lifestyle risk behaviours, self-reported cardiometabolic conditions and preventive practices, and examine selected lifestyle correlates of self-reported diabetes and hypertension among women attending Kasoa Polyclinic, Ghana. Methods. A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted in June and July 2024 among 174 women aged 18-45 years recruited by convenience sampling. A structured, interviewer-assisted questionnaire covered knowledge, lifestyle behaviours, self-reported diagnoses and preventive practices. Data were summarised as frequencies and percentages, and associations were examined with Pearson's chi-square test. Results. Only 37 women (21.3%) described metabolic syndrome as a condition that raises the risk of heart disease and type 2 diabetes, 40 (23.0%) identified central (apple-shaped) fat as the high-risk pattern and 31 (17.8%) knew that dietary recommendations exist. Most reported no weekly physical activity (116; 66.7%), daily sugary drinks (109; 62.6%), daily processed or fast food (100; 57.5%), high stress (103; 59.2%), and less than six hours' sleep (94; 54.0%). Self-reported diagnoses were hypertension in 60 (34.5%) and type 2 diabetes in 49 (28.2%). Fifty-nine (33.9%) had never received advice on prevention and 105 (60.3%) did not monitor their weight or waist. Self-reported diabetes was associated with short sleep (36.2% among those sleeping under six hours; p = 0.035) and with stress level (p = 0.028), being most frequent among women reporting low stress. Self-reported hypertension was more common with high stress (42.7%; p = 0.022) and with some physical activity (p = 0.005). Conclusion. Women attending this polyclinic appeared to have limited understanding of metabolic syndrome and a high burden of modifiable risk behaviours. Routine counselling on diet, activity, sleep, and weight monitoring at the polyclinic may be warranted. The bivariate, self-reported associations should be interpreted cautiously.

papers.title: Levodopa Preferentially Reorganizes Dorsal Subthalamic Activity in Parkinsons Disease
papers.abstract: Background: Dopamine replacement reshapes subthalamic activity in Parkinson's disease, but whether this response reflects anatomically organized network reconfiguration remains unclear. Objectives: To determine whether levodopa preferentially reorganizes dorsal subthalamic spectral activity and cortico-subthalamic directionality. Methods: Twelve participants undergoing bilateral subthalamic deep brain stimulation contributed 30 contacts (14 dorsal, 16 ventral). Recordings obtained OFF and ON medication underwent spectral parameterization and multiband state-space analysis. Simultaneous electroencephalography in six participants enabled assessment of directional cortico-subthalamic coupling using the phase slope index. Results: Levodopa suppressed beta power more strongly dorsally than ventrally (-2.473 versus -0.120 dB; p=0.0438). Dorsal theta power increased, with a trend toward an increase after baseline normalization (p=0.07). Dorsal contacts exhibited greater theta-beta (+5.904 versus +1.610 dB; p=0.006) and gamma-beta (+2.516 versus +0.384 dB; p=0.0188) state-space shifts, principally driven by beta suppression. Gamma changes did not differ regionally. Concurrently, dorsal low-beta and beta interactions shifted toward cortical leading at selected electrodes, whereas ventral responses were less consistent. Conclusions: Levodopa produces a topographically organized subthalamic response, combining preferential dorsal beta suppression with altered cortico-subthalamic directionality. These findings position contact anatomy as a key consideration in characterizing dopaminergic network responses and motivate clinical validation of spatially informed multiband biomarkers for adaptive stimulation.

papers.title: Cognition, Lifestyles, and Environments: Quantifying the Roles of Body Physiology and the Brain
papers.abstract: Lifestyle and environmental factors are increasingly promoted as modifiable targets for maintaining cognitive health. Yet, it remains unclear how well they predict cognitive functioning and to what extent their associations with cognition are reflected in brain and body measures. We applied machine learning to multimodal data from over 10,000 UK Biobank participants to evaluate the predictive value of twelve lifestyle and environment domains, spanning physical activity, diet, smoking, alcohol consumption, sleep, sexual behavior, electronic device use, and environmental exposures, for cognition, both individually and in combination, and quantified the extent to which these associations are captured by body and brain. A model integrating lifestyle and environment domains explained 23% of the variance in cognition at r=0.48, comparable to body and brain markers. Physical activity, diet, alcohol consumption, sun exposure, and local environment emerged as the strongest predictors. A composite brain marker integrating three neuroimaging modalities accounted for 57.7% of the lifestyle-cognition association, while a composite body marker spanning nine physiological systems accounted for 47.8%. Jointly, lifestyle, environment, body, and brain captured 92.6% of age-related cognitive variation. Therefore, integrating lifestyle and environmental factors enables robust prediction of cognition within the UK Biobank cohort, and much of this association is reflected in brain and bodily health. However, the generalizability of these findings to broader populations requires further evaluation.

papers.title: Effects of Cannabidiol on Auditory Mismatch Negativity in Autistic Children
papers.abstract: Pharmacological treatments targeting core autistic features remain limited. In neurotypical adults, cannabidiol (CBD) alters mismatch negativity (MMN), an electrophysiological marker of automatic auditory deviance detection that has been associated with autistic traits. The effects of CBD on MMN, as measured using electroencephalography (EEG), in autistic children remain unknown. This secondary analysis of a pilot randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial examined the effects of 12 weeks of oral CBD oil on MMN during a duration-deviant auditory oddball task. We hypothesised that CBD would produce more negative MMN amplitudes and shorter peak latencies relative to placebo. Nineteen autistic children (6-12 years, 8 female) received CBD (dose) and placebo in randomised order, separated by an 8-week washout. Age-adjusted linear mixed-effects models tested Time (baseline, follow-up) x Treatment (CBD, placebo) effects on mean MMN amplitude and peak latency separately at Fz and FCz. Exploratory Spearman correlations examined baseline associations between MMN and Developmental Behaviour Checklist-2 (DBC-2) Social Relating scores. At FCz, latency decreased following CBD but increased following placebo but did not survive FDR correction (p = .029, pFDR = .058) and no other interactions were significant. Higher baseline DBC-2 Social Relating scores were associated with more negative MMN amplitude at FCz (rho = -.58, pFDR = .028) and Fz (rho = -.59, pFDR = .028). These findings provide tentative evidence that CBD may modulate MMN latency in autistic children. Larger trials should clarify CBDs effects on MMN and further examine the association between MMN amplitude and social-relating difficulties.
